cards.body:
*Lesson 3.2 · Items & Expressions*

_≈ 2 hours · with Miracle_

This is the module that makes n8n click. Data moves between nodes as a list of *items*, and *expressions* let any field reach into that data, including data from nodes further back. Get these two ideas right and most "why is it doing that?" moments in n8n disappear.

*Your problem:* n8n's data model of items and expressions trips everyone up at first.
*The plan:* Learn how items flow and write expressions to reach any value.
*After this lesson:* You can move and transform data in n8n confidently.

*Three orders, one name*

*Wednesday:* Tolu's new workflow writes delivery messages for tomorrow's three orders. All three greet Mrs Adebayo.

*Mr Okafor:* The one message that was sent went to the wrong person. Worse: it showed another customer's order.

*Nodo:* "Every node passes a list of items. Each item must stay matched to its own customer all the way down the line."

*Glitch:* "I swapped one word in the expression. Now every item looks at the first customer. Find me."

*Items: n8n's unit of data*

Between nodes, n8n always passes a *list of items*. Each item is one record (one order, one row, one email) and holds its fields under `json`. Most nodes *run once for each item* they receive, and they keep track of which input item each output came from. n8n calls this *item linking* (or paired items).

*Weave:* Items are my bundles under another name. The big difference: in n8n, items don't cost anything extra. The whole run is one execution.

*Expressions and $json*

An expression is JavaScript inside `{{ }}`, in a field switched to *Expression* mode. The most used variable is `$json`: *the current item's data from the node directly before this one*.
Code example on screen (Expressions and $json): open it in the app.

You rarely type these by hand. *Drag a field from the Input panel* into a parameter and n8n writes the expression. The preview under the field shows the result for the current item. Read it every time.

*Reaching back: $('Node')*

`$json` only sees the node directly before. To use data from further back, name the node:

_Expression · Gives you · Use it when_
- `$('Orders').item.json.total` · The Orders item *linked to the current item* · Almost always. Each message gets its own order.
- `$('Orders').first().json.total` · The *first* Orders item, for every item · Only when there's one shared value, such as a settings row
- `$('Orders').last().json.total` · The last Orders item · Rarely; for example, the newest row
- `$('Orders').all()` · Every Orders item as a list · Totals and summaries, e.g. `.all().length`
- `$input.item.json` · Same as `$json` · When you want to be explicit
- `$itemIndex` · The current item's position (0, 1, 2…) · Numbering and debugging

*Try it.* The node "Build message" is running. Its input comes from "Find customer". Edit the template and watch all three items.
Hands-on lab: Reaching back: $('Node'). It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Formatting dates, numbers and text*

Expressions are JavaScript, so ordinary string and number methods work. For dates, n8n includes the *Luxon* library: `$now` and `$today` are Luxon dates, and `DateTime` turns text into one.
Code example on screen (Formatting dates, numbers and text): open it in the app.
*Nodo:* If an expression grows longer than one line, it belongs in a Code node (3.5). Expressions are for small, readable transformations.

*Pin test data*

Every time you click Execute, n8n calls the real APIs again: slow, sometimes costly, and the data changes under you. *Pinning* freezes a node's output. Click the pin icon in a node's Output panel and n8n reuses that output instead of running the node again. You can also edit pinned data to create test cases, such as a customer with no phone number.

- *Pinned data is for building*: n8n uses pinned data only in manual runs from the editor. Published, automatic runs always use real data.
- *Edit to test edge cases*: Add an item with a missing field or a huge total, and check that every expression downstream copes.
- *Unpin when the shape changes*: If you add a column to the sheet, stale pinned data won't have it, and you'll chase a bug that isn't there.

cards.body:
*Solved problem: a WhatsApp-ready message for every order*

*The goal.* Each evening, Tolu wants a ready-to-send WhatsApp message for every order delivering tomorrow, with the customer's name, order number, items, total and delivery day, plus a one-tap link that opens WhatsApp with the message filled in. Order data lives in the *Orders* sheet; names and phones live in *Customers*. Sending automatically comes later (Boss 3); for now the messages go into an *Outbox* sheet.

*Step 1 · Get tomorrow's orders*

Start with a *Manual Trigger* (swap in a Schedule Trigger at 18:00 once it works). Add *Google Sheets · Get Row(s)*, rename the node *Orders*, and add a filter: column `delivery_date` equals
Code example on screen (Get tomorrow's orders): open it in the app.
Execute the step. With three orders for tomorrow, the Output says *3 items*. Now *pin* this output. From here on you build without touching the sheet.

*Step 2 · Look up each customer*

Add another *Get Row(s)* on the Customers sheet and rename it *Find customer*. Filter: `customer_id` equals `{{ $json.customer_id }}` (drag it from the Input panel). Execute: the node runs *once per order* and outputs three items, each linked to its order. Pin this too.

*Nodo:* *Rename nodes before you reference them.* Expressions use node names, so "Orders" beats "Google Sheets1". n8n updates references when you rename a node in the editor, but expressions you paste in from elsewhere won't know the new name.

*Step 3 · Build the message with Edit Fields*

Add *Edit Fields (Set)*, rename it *Build message*, and add three fields. Its input is Find customer, so `$json` is the customer; the order is reached through `$('Orders').item`:

_(Code on screen in the app.)_

Check the preview under the field, then use the arrows in the Input panel to step through items 0, 1 and 2: each preview must show a different customer *and* their own order.

*Step 4 · Add the one-tap WhatsApp link*

Add a fourth field, `wa_link`. WhatsApp's click-to-chat links need the number without the plus sign, and the text URL-encoded:

_(Code on screen in the app.)_

To put the *full* message in the link, you'd want to reuse the `message` field, but fields in the same Edit Fields node can't see each other. Add a second Edit Fields node after this one (with *Include Other Input Fields* on) and set `wa_link` there, using `{{ encodeURIComponent($json.message) }}` as the text.

*Step 5 · Write to the Outbox and test the edge cases*

Add *Google Sheets · Append Row* on an Outbox sheet with columns `order_id · phone · message · wa_link`, mapped automatically. Then edit the pinned Orders data to add a fourth order whose `customer_id` doesn't exist, and run again. Find customer returns nothing for that item, so it silently disappears. Fix it: in Find customer's *Settings*, turn on *Always Output Data*, and in Build message use `{{ $json.name ?? 'Customer' }}`. Then Tolu sees the order and can fix the customer record.

- *1* execution for the whole evening run
- *4* orders, 4 messages, 0 mix-ups
- *0* API calls while building, thanks to pinning

*Why this approach works*

- `.item` keeps every message matched to its own order through item linking.
- Clear node names make expressions readable months later.
- Pinned data makes testing fast and repeatable, and lets you invent edge cases.
- Stepping through every item in the preview catches mix-ups before customers do.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Using `.first()` where you meant `.item`.
- Checking only item 0 in the preview.
- Field names in the wrong case: `Name` isn't `name`.
- Forgetting that a lookup with no result drops the item.
- Leaving stale pinned data after changing the sheet's columns.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* Five broken outboxes. Use the simulator in Card 3 to test your theories.

*A:* All three messages greet Mrs Adebayo, but each shows the correct order number.
*B:* An expression copied from a YouTube tutorial fails with `Referenced node "Google Sheets" doesn't exist`.
*C:* The message says `for [Object: {"order_id":"HL-0071",…}]`.
*D:* Tolu added tomorrow's new orders to the sheet, clicked Execute workflow, and the Outbox still shows yesterday's three.
*E:* Four orders go in, three messages come out. No error anywhere.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* the name uses `$('Find customer').first()`, which is always item 0. Use `$json.name` (or `$('Find customer').item`). The order number used `.item`, which is why it was right.
*B:* the expression names a node that isn't in this workflow. Change it to your node's name, `$('Orders')`.
*C:* the expression returns a whole object, `$('Orders').item.json`. Add the field you need: `.json.items`.
*D:* Orders still has pinned data from yesterday, and manual runs use it. Unpin it (or re-execute that node), then pin the fresh output.
*E:* one order's `customer_id` has no match, so Find customer outputs nothing for it and the item disappears. Turn on Always Output Data and handle the empty customer, or flag the order for Tolu.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): Build on pinned data
cards.body:
- Build the solved workflow. Pin Orders and Find customer after their first run.
- Edit the pinned data to add two edge cases: a customer with no `area`, and an order with a total of 250,000.
- Run the workflow five times without either Sheets node calling Google.

*Done when:*
- Every message in the Outbox has the right name, order and formatted total, including the edge cases.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): Five formatting expressions
cards.body:
- Write and test expressions that produce: tomorrow's date as "Tuesday 6 October"; a total as "₦34,000"; 7.5% VAT rounded to the nearest naira; a phone number in local format (080…); and "Free delivery" for orders of ₦30,000 or more.
- Paste each expression and its output for two different items into your log.

*Done when:*
- All five give correct results for both items, and none uses `.first()`.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): Three sources, one message
cards.body:
- Add a third sheet, *Riders* (area, rider_name, rider_phone), and a node that finds the rider for each customer's area.
- Extend the message so it includes data from three different earlier nodes: the order, the customer and the rider ("Your rider is Musa, 0803…").
- Make it survive a missing rider: the message should say "Rider to be assigned" instead of breaking.

*Done when:*
- All items are correct with five test orders across at least three areas, including one area with no rider. You can explain which expression reads from which node.

cards.q: A Google Sheets node outputs 4 items into a node that sends an email. How many emails?
cards.why: Most nodes run once for each item they receive.

cards.q: In a node whose input comes from "Find customer", what is `$json`?
options: The current item from Find customer
The first item of the trigger
cards.why: $json is the current item's data from the node directly before.

cards.q: Every message shows the same customer. Which expression is the likely culprit?
cards.why: .first() returns item 0 every time. .item follows the link to the matching item.

cards.q: Does a published workflow use pinned data when its schedule fires?
options: No, pinned data is only used in manual runs
cards.why: Pinning is a building tool. Automatic runs always fetch real data.
DateTime.fromISO parses the text; toFormat with cccc d LLL formats it. $now would give today, not the delivery date.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Data travels as a list of items; most nodes run once per item.
2. `$json` is the current item from the node directly before.
3. `$('Node').item` follows the item link back; `.first()` is item 0 for everyone.
4. Name nodes clearly before you reference them.
5. Format with JavaScript and Luxon; move long logic to a Code node.
6. Pin data to build fast; unpin when the data's shape changes.
7. Step through every item in the preview, not just the first.

*Lesson 3.2 complete!* _Items & Expressions_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 3.3, _Flow Control_.
